Calcitriol (active vitamin D: cholecalciferol → 25-OH in liver → 1,25-(OH)₂ in kidney via PTH-driven 1α-hydroxylase) is the effector
arm. Calcitonin (thyroid C-cells) plays only a minor calcium-lowering role; severe hypomagnesaemia paradoxically suppresses PTH.
Releases calcium AND phosphate from bone
No direct action on the gut
Serum calcium ↑ and serum phosphate ↓ — the phosphaturic action is why primary hyperparathyroidism gives a HIGH calcium
inferior glands may be ectopic → thymus / mediastinum
4th pharyngeal pouch; migrate little — constant, posterior to the RLN plane.
3rd pouch; descend with the thymus — variable, anterior to the RLN; ectopic in
Mainly the inferior thyroid artery (both pairs) — preserve it at thyroidectomy.
Usually four glands; supernumerary glands in ~13%.
PRIMARY vs SECONDARY vs TERTIARY — THE BIOCHEMISTRY
CAUSES OF HYPERCALCAEMIA — CHECK THE PTH
Granulomatous (sarcoid, TB), thyrotoxicosis, thiazides, vitamin D/A,
Primary hyperparathyroidism and malignancy together cause ~90% of hypercalcaemia — the PTH level splits them: high/normal =
PTH raises calcium but LOWERS phosphate — a high calcium with a low phosphate is the classic primary-HPT fingerprint.
Superior glands come from the 4th pouch (migrate least — high and constant); inferior glands come from the 3rd pouch and
descend with the thymus, so ectopic inferior glands hide in the mediastinum.
Both pairs are usually supplied by the inferior thyroid artery — preserve it during thyroidectomy to avoid devascularising the
Secondary HPT is an APPROPRIATE response to low calcium (high PTH, low/normal calcium); tertiary is autonomous with a HIGH
Severe hypomagnesaemia suppresses PTH release — the hypocalcaemia will not correct until magnesium is replaced.
Sources: standard physiology & surgical anatomy texts · Society for Endocrinology · NICE NG132 (hyperparathyroidism classification).
CaSR = calcium-sensing receptor; RLN = recurrent laryngeal nerve. Diagnosis, sestamibi localisation and parathyroidectomy are on sheet 2 of 2.
